papers.authors: Minyong Cho, Minho Jeong, Dooho Lee, Jinmo Lee, Jaemin Yoo
papers.evidence: Causilo是位于性能-效率帕累托前沿的表格基础模型
papers.tldr: 表格基础模型常难以兼顾前沿预测性能与推理效率。Causilo 在 TabICL 列-行架构上新增行精炼模块，让列编码后的单元表示先在行内交互，再经一次列阶段后压缩为行嵌入，两阶段均用固定数量摘要 token 的交叉注意力，使注意力开销随特征数线性增长。模型在约 3600 万合成表上预训练，于 TabArena 取得 1785.4 Elo，每 1K 测试样本中位推理仅 0.10 秒，比 TabPFN-3.5-Fast 快 31.6%，同时位列性能-效率帕累托前沿。
papers.abstract_en: We introduce Causilo, a tabular foundation model (TFM) that combines frontier predictive performance with exceptionally fast inference. On TabArena, Causilo achieves 1785.4 Elo, at a median inference time of 0.10 seconds per 1K test samples. It outperforms TabPFN-3.5-Fast with 31.6% less inference time, placing it on the performance--efficiency Pareto frontier. Causilo follows TabICL's column-then-row architecture but introduces another row-refinement module before row compression. This module exchanges information among cell representations within each row after column encoding. The refined cells then visit the context set again through an additional column stage before being compressed into row embeddings. For inference efficiency, both row stages use cross-attention through a fixed number of summary tokens, keeping their attention cost linear in the number of features. Pretrained on approximately 36M synthetic tables, Causilo delivers strong benchmark results across TabArena, BeyondArena, and ScoringBench, achieving frontier-level performance with substantially faster inference.

papers.title_en: PACE: Plug-and-Play Contextual Embedding for Feature Screening with Pretrained Tabular Foundation Models
papers.authors: Qi Qin, Erbo Li, Ting Wei, Zizhou Huang, Zixuan Qin, Wu Wang, Yifan Sun
papers.evidence: 利用预训练表格基础模型进行特征筛选
papers.tldr: 高维表格学习中，特征筛选常直接对原始值打分，容易忽略非线性与分布结构。PACE将冻结的表格基础模型列编码器插入现有筛选规则前，把每个特征扩展为高维上下文表示。受控实验显示，它能以较小编码开销提升复杂非线性依赖的筛选效果；在TALENT下游任务中，PACE-DC使二分类AUC提升0.077、多分类宏AUC提升0.064，十个学习器归一化RMSE中位改善0.063。随机权重与随机特征对照表明，增益来自预训练结构而非单纯维度扩展。
papers.abstract_en: In high-dimensional tabular learning, feature screening provides a lightweight, model-agnostic way to remove irrelevant features before model fitting. However, scoring raw values directly can miss nonlinear or distributional structure. We introduce PACE (Plug-and-Play Contextual Embedding), which inserts a frozen tabular foundation model (TFM) column encoder before an existing feature-scoring rule, expanding each feature into a higher-dimensional contextual representation. Across controlled studies, PACE improves raw-space screening of complex nonlinear dependence with only modest additional encoding cost. These gains translate to downstream prediction on TALENT datasets: PACE-DC improves binary AUC by 0.077 and multiclass macro-AUC by 0.064, with a median normalized RMSE improvement of 0.063 across ten learners. Matched random-weight and random-feature controls show that PACE gains from pretrained structure beyond generic dimensional expansion. PACE further achieves favorable performance--time trade-offs against task-fitted selectors and attribution-based methods, positioning pretrained column geometry as a reusable upstream primitive for tabular learning.

papers.title_en: Enhancing Transformer Representations of Symbolic ODE Expressions
papers.authors: Xiyue Fan, Adam Prugel-Bennett, Stuart E. Middleton
papers.evidence: 符号回归与符号表达式结构化表示
papers.tldr: 符号微分方程通常以表达式树表示，但Transformer的标准位置编码面向序列，难以有效捕捉其层次结构。本文系统研究树位置编码在符号ODE任务中的作用，并在学习到的结构表示上引入对比学习以支持数学交换律。实验表明，树位置编码在早期训练即有助益，且随训练持续提升，在不同数据规模和任务上均带来稳定优势。消融实验进一步揭示这些方法如何协同建模符号数学结构。
papers.abstract_en: Existing approaches to solving differential equations, such as symbolic regression, physics informed neural networks, and neural operators, typically focus on numerical approximations or blind symbolic search via fitting to numerical data. Less attention has been paid to learning structured representations of mathematical expressions that preserve commutative properties and could support mathematical reasoning in symbolic forms. Transformer models have shown strong capabilities in solving symbolic differential equations. However, standard positional embeddings in transformers are designed for sequence data. Symbolic differential equations are naturally represented by expression trees, so these positional embeddings may not efficiently capture their hierarchical structures. We investigate existing tree positional embeddings in symbolic ordinary differential equation (ODE) tasks. We systematically study their effectiveness under different settings. Our results show that tree positional embeddings aid learning in early epochs and continue to improve performance throughout, ultimately yielding consistent advantages across various data sizes and tasks. Based on learned structural representations, we apply contrastive learning to support the commutative property in mathematics. Ablation studies provide insight into how these methods interact in modelling symbolic mathematical structures.
